precepts.text: The canonical book names the same Mardocheus, a Benjamite carried away from Jerusalem with Jeconiah by Nebuchadnezzar, the very account the Apocrypha references.
precepts.point: Mardocheus was one of the captives whom Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon carried from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Judea. This same captivity and lineage are named in the canonical book, which proves the Apocrypha runs right along with the rest of the Bible.
precepts.why:
Mardocheus is set out by his line and his captivity: “Mardocheus the son of Jairus, the son of Semei, the son of Cisai, of the tribe of Benjamin”, a Jew who “dwelt in the city of Susa, a great man, being a servitor in the king’s court”, and “one of the captives, which Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon carried from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Judea”.

The canonical book names the same man the same way: “Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite; Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.” Jairus is Jair, Semei is Shimei, Cisai is Kish; Susa is Shushan, Jechonias is Jeconiah, Nabuchodonosor is Nebuchadnezzar. One Benjamite, one captivity, one account.

That is the proof that the Apocrypha runs right along with the rest of the Bible. The dream of Mardocheus is not a story off to the side; it references the very captivity and lineage the canonical book records.

points: The chapter opens with a note that in the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemeus and Cleopatra, Dositheus, said to be a priest and Levite, and his son Ptolemeus, brought this epistle of Purim, which was interpreted by Lysimachus in Jerusalem.

In the second year of the reign of Artexerxes the great, on the first day of the month Nisan, Mardocheus the son of Jairus, of the tribe of Benjamin, had a dream. He was a Jew dwelling in the city of Susa, a great man and a servitor in the king's court.

Mardocheus was one of the captives whom Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon carried from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Judea. This same captivity and lineage are named in the canonical book, which proves the Apocrypha runs right along with the rest of the Bible.

Mardocheus saw a noise of tumult, with thunder, earthquakes, and uproar in the land, and two great dragons came forth ready to fight, and their cry was great. These are the two dragons already named as Mardocheus and Aman.

At their cry all nations were prepared to battle against the righteous people, and there came a day of darkness, tribulation, anguish, and great uproar upon the earth, and the whole righteous nation was troubled and ready to perish.

Then they cried unto the Most High, and upon their cry, as from a little fountain, was made a great flood of much water. That little fountain is Esther. The light and the sun rose up, the lowly were exalted, and they devoured the glorious.

When Mardocheus awoke, knowing what the Most High had determined to do, he kept the dream in mind and desired all night by every means to understand it. He wanted to know the meaning of the two dragons, the uproar of the nations, the cry of Israel, and the waters.
